question: Does the frozen skip-guard analyzer identify useful state-masking candidates beyond simple file-level triage in a fixed new source cohort?
selection: Purposive established Python/native-extension projects outside the prior 30-package selected-source inventory. Not random, independent human selection, or guaranteed previously unseen in broader research history. No replacement for unavailable repositories.
revision_rule: Default branch HEAD resolved once before source download, then pinned commit used.
eligibility: Every UTF-8 .py regular file <=1MB in pinned archive, with test in any path component or basename conftest.py. Retain all eligible file records including those without query text. No exclusion for negative results.

baselines.direct_ast: direct function/class skipif query and direct negated query assertion, no aliases/helpers

analysis_rule: Freeze implementation. Analyze all eligible files containing skipif; record parse/errors and no-query files. File-level warning counts are triage counts, not accuracy. Inspect every analyzer-positive file and all cooccurrence-positive misses. No execution of third-party suites in this phase.
decision: If no additional confirmed practical value is found, do not claim publication readiness. Source candidates alone require full-suite/context verification. Baseline-negative files are not ground-truth negatives.
bounds: 8 repositories, at most 60MB compressed each. No replacement or cherry-picking.
